audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted their own whys in both layers. Level 1 said Jax although whys[0] says 'concede the level'; Level 2 said Skill although whys[1] says 'she still edges the level'; Level 3 said Quinn although whys[2] calls it 'a genuine coinflip'; first item said Quinn although whys[5] says it 'tips back to a coinflip'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Quinn / Quinn / Skill / Quinn / Jax / Skill / Quinn and matches the prose exactly. At 48.2% Jax has one real window — level 6 with Grandmaster's Might — and loses the poke phases on either side of it.
audit.corrected: phases[0]/win[0] Quinn, phases[1]/win[1] Quinn, phases[2]/win[2] Skill, phases[5]/win[5] Skill — matched pairs, ratings realigned.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys carried no cooldowns; the Level 6 row was generic boilerplate on the one stage that decides the lane.
audit.why: Vault is 12/11/10/9/8s and is her only repositioning tool — baiting it empty is the entire all-in condition. Blinding Assault is 11s at rank 1. Grandmaster's Might is 110s. Those three numbers are the matchup.
audit.corrected: Phase whys rebuilt around Vault's 12s and Blinding Assault's 11s, with Level 6 stated as the bait-then-leap window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate written as 'Grandmaster at Arms' in whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid, late and wants.you[2] — five fields. Vault is described only as a reposition; Riot's text says it also briefly interrupts the target.
audit.why: Fabricated ability name repeated five times on one page. The interrupt matters: Vault can knock Jax out of his own commit, which is a second reason to force it before engaging rather than during. The page's blind coverage is already correct — Blinding Assault makes Jax's autos miss, so Counter Strike's dodge has nothing to negate and Relentless Assault never ramps.
audit.corrected: Grandmaster's Might in all five; Vault's brief interrupt stated in the Levels 4-5 phase.

audit.why: The page correctly identifies Vault as the punishable cooldown and the all-in condition; it simply never gave the number.
audit.corrected: 12s at rank 1 now stated in the Level 6 phase and mid.

edits.before: Auto-trade only with E held in your pocket. Identify how Quinn contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Hers: Harrier-marked autos chunk you for free and Vault repositions her out of range. Last-hit and take the chip.

edits.before: Counter Strike flips every AA exchange he starts. Only take the trade when Quinn's Vault is down.
edits.after: Blinding Assault (11s) makes your autos whiff, so your burst never lands cleanly and she still edges it.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Quinn must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike is your first answer, but it only pays if she commits autos into it — ranged poke never feeds the stun.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Vault's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still hers: she pokes without stepping into E range, and Vault briefly interrupts you, so it breaks your commit as well as the gap.

edits.after: Your one window: force Vault (12s at rank 1) empty, Leap Strike in, and Grandmaster's Might's resists win the extended duel.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 still belong to her because she pokes from range without ever feeding Counter Strike and kites on her Harrier passive move-speed. But level 6 is your window and the whole lane hinges on it: Grandmaster at Arms hands you the Armor/MR active plus the on-hit ramp, so if you bait her Vault (E) out and Leap Strike onto her while it's down, you eat her Harrier burst and win the extended duel cleanly. The trick is landing the gap-close — Vault is her only repositioning tool, so force it empty before you commit Q and R, or she just dashes off and the all-in collapses.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 still belong to her because she pokes from range without ever feeding Counter Strike and kites on her Harrier passive move-speed. But level 6 is your window and the whole lane hinges on it: Grandmaster's Might hands you the Armor/MR active plus the on-hit ramp, so if you bait her Vault (E, 12s at rank 1) out and Leap Strike onto her while it's down, you eat her Harrier burst and win the extended duel cleanly. Vault is her only reposition and it briefly interrupts you on the way out, so force it empty before you commit Q and R, or the all-in collapses.

edits.before: If you didn't convert your level 6-8 window, this lane drifts away from you. Quinn out-roams everything once her ult (Behind Enemy Lines) is up, and her lethality build pokes you off the side wave without ever stepping into Counter Strike (E) range. You still win the rare straight 1v1 if you ever pin her with Grandmaster at Arms active and your stun landed — but she won't give you one. She'll poke, Vault out, and leave to make plays bot or mid. Snowball the level 6 all-in into her tower or a kill so her lethality scaling and roam pressure never get to matter.
edits.after: If you didn't convert your level 6-8 window, this lane drifts away from you. Snowball the level 6 all-in into her tower or a kill so her lethality scaling and roam pressure never get to matter.

notes: 'Grandmaster at Arms' appeared in five separate fields on this page — the worst instance of that error in my slice. Four chart rows also disagreed with their own whys. Added Vault's brief interrupt (it breaks Jax's commit, not just the gap) which the page omitted. Data note: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json lists Behind Enemy Lines' cooldown as 3s — that is the recast/Skystrike value, not the ultimate's real cooldown, so I wrote no R cooldown for her rather than repeat a bad number.
